Videos were deliberately deleted before this assignment. All7 contact sheets and25 listed fullframes were actually viewed. No video inspected, recovered or downloaded. Fullframe positions occasionally obscure symbols; neighboring listed frames resolve all relied-on formulas.

Board L18A f0054/f0060 writes (p1-p2)/rho_f=g h without connected-liquid-leg correction. Chapter derives (rho_m-rho)g Delta h; rho_m g Delta h only when leg density negligible. This is an explicit correction, not an unverified transcription.

Publisher caption L18A1444.56-1469.28 says V2 divided by rho for pressure term; board f0050 clearly p2/rho. L18B1216.16-1231.36 garbles root operation; board f0048/f0051 and direct algebra establish V=sqrt[2(p0-p)/rho].

Lecture Cd sketch/illustrative values (Venturi above0.9, orifice about0.6), size/cost ranking and sample probe dimensions remain attributed examples; not adopted as universal specifications. No commercial performance or empirical correlation asserted.

The cooling-line values, rho/mu/rho_m, calibration datum, uncertainty bounds, loss and exercise calibration law are constructed inputs; no temperature-specific property claims, measured validation or empirical range invented.

NBS1984 is accessible government engineering guidance; its p.9 Table1 compiles referenced device-specific loss estimates. Underlying original experiments and current standards not consulted; only metering-versus-permanent-loss distinction used. NASA HTML has named-section locators rather than page numbers.

No unsteady Bernoulli extension asserted. The finite-reservoir example is expressly quasi-steady; global B proof uses zero gradient on a connected region, not an unjustified global velocity potential.

No dependency on unaccepted Chapter8; equations and assumptions used are restated. No cross-chapter local links are required in this standalone draft. Shared build/browser validation and independent review are pending.

sections.section: The measurement question and its formal model
sections.teaching_construction: Cooling-line model with specified liquid/geometry/duty; definitions of streamline, tube, control volume, uniform versus bulk speed.

sections.section: From a stream tube to mechanical energy
sections.lecture_material: Steady constant-density uniform-port engineering energy balance; thin stream tube; no flow across sides; inviscid, no shaft work, mechanical energy and pressure-flow work.
sections.teaching_construction: Explicit pressure-work-per-mass construction; explains that thin geometry removes neither shear work nor a shaft source.

sections.section: Deriving the streamline invariant from momentum
sections.lecture_material: Statement that Bernoulli can also be derived from the steady inviscid momentum equation; projectile contrast.
sections.teaching_construction: Full Euler projection/integration, conservative force potential, streamline constant, stagnation limit, constant density restriction and numerical/hydrostatic/equal-area checks.

sections.section: When the constant can be shared across streamlines
sections.teaching_construction: Vorticity identity and connected-region global constant proof; solid-body rotational counterexample and numerical check; wall pressure/core velocity qualification.

sections.section: Energy, pressure and head: choosing the two points
sections.teaching_construction: Three energy units; datum and gauge invariance; free-jet pressure justification, Torricelli construction, finite reservoir correction and quasi-steady boundary.

sections.section: The Venturi meter: turning pressure into flow
sections.lecture_material: Converging/throat/diverging geometry, pressure taps, favorable/adverse gradients; equal-height Bernoulli plus mass balance.
sections.teaching_construction: Algebra including beta^4, limiting/conditioning checks, computed geometry/head Figure9.1, cooling-line ideal flow, unequal-height correction.

sections.section: What a differential manometer actually measures
sections.lecture_material: U-tube differential measurement with different manometer and flowing densities; ideal flow expression.
sections.teaching_construction: Full pressure walk corrects missing leg-density contribution; chosen rho_m numerical check, zero-density-difference limit, unequal-tap elevation relation.

sections.section: Discharge coefficient and a calibration that depends on flow
sections.lecture_material: Viscous/nonuniform correction via Cd, independent calibration, Cd versus inlet Re and iteration; practical length/cost tradeoff.
sections.research_extension: NBS BSS159 pp.4,10-11 calibration and conditions.
sections.teaching_construction: Fixed versus implicit coefficient model, derivative convergence condition, running-case actual flow/Re, effective throat discrepancy distinguished from permanent loss.

sections.section: Pressure recovery, separation and mechanical-energy loss
sections.lecture_material: Adverse pressure gradient, separation, eddies, reduced effective forward-flow area, mechanical energy ultimately internal.
sections.research_extension: NBS BSS159 p.9 Table1 differentiates permanent loss from meter differential.
sections.teaching_construction: Steady engineering head budget with separate pump/turbine/loss terms and derived alpha flux weighting; hypothetical downstream pressure/power check.

sections.section: Orifice meters, the vena contracta and flow nozzles
sections.lecture_material: Plate, separated jet, vena contracta, pressure taps, illustrative Cd about0.6 versus Venturi above0.9; curved flow-nozzle contour; practical tradeoffs.
sections.teaching_construction: Geometric versus vena-contracta area and coefficients, wall-tap limitation, double-correction diagnostic, Cd not efficiency. Lecture comparisons explicitly attributed/qualified.

sections.lecture_material: Pitot streamline stagnation, p0/p/dynamic pressure, speed inversion; Pitot-static separate ports, sample dimensions, alignment and multiple-hole option.
sections.research_extension: NASA Glenn named sections: separate passages, differential inversion and measurement limitations.
sections.teaching_construction: Ideal point/height assumptions, Figure9.2, running-case differential, parabolic traverse counterexample, quantitative signal sensitivity.
Constructed bounded calibration/differential/throat uncertainties, log sensitivities, nonlinear corner interval and conditional duty decision.

sections.section: Executable inverse model and failure checks
sections.teaching_construction: Fresh-process standard-library inverse/forward flow, continuity/Bernoulli, corner sweep, manometer walk, rotational check, omitted-denominator mutation and rejected invalid geometry.

sections.section: What the model captures and what it misses
sections.teaching_construction: Explicit theorem/calibration/head-balance boundaries; maps inviscid/uniform/steady/constant-density omissions to needed input.

sections.lecture_material: Uses lecture instrumentation as problem context.
sections.teaching_construction: Six fully solved varied original exercises: inclined inverse meter; rotational local stagnation; implicit calibration/contraction; nozzle boundary/loss; power design; profile traverse and alpha.

symbol_ledger.definition: Specified density/dynamic viscosity, section diameters/areas/static pressures, inlet-minus-throat pressure difference, volume flow rate.
Position/time/velocity/speed/elevation, gravitational magnitude/upward unit vector, downstream area normal and bulk speed.
Volume transported through a steady constant-density streamtube in dt; matches book volume convention.
Body force per mass; conservative potential; arc length; streamline unit tangent; mechanical-energy invariant per mass; streamline-specific constant.
Vorticity curl V; rigid-body angular rate; cylindrical radius/radial/azimuthal vectors; p_c is pressure at the axis reference point r=0,z=0.
Total head B/g; gauge/atmospheric pressure; reservoir head; jet speed/area and reservoir area/surface speed.
D2/D1; ideal inverse-meter volume flow rate.
Manometer density, interface/tap elevations, interface-height difference and interface pressures.
Discharge ratio, Reynolds number using upstream bulk speed and diameter, a calibrated coefficient function.
Pump head added, turbine head extracted, irreversible mechanical loss, kinetic-energy correction, axial normal speed, recovered-outlet pressure.
Vena-contracta area, geometric opening area, vena-contracta pressure, contraction ratio Ac/Ao.
Stagnation pressure; stagnation-point elevation minus upstream-point elevation; radius and centre-line maximum in the explicitly defined parabolic profile.
a=4rho/(pi mu D1) in Exercise3; positive profile exponent n in Exercise6.
